sources.entry: django-allauth - Authentication app for Django that "just works."

summary.one_liner: django-allauth is an integrated set of Django apps covering local registration, login, account management, and third-party (social) login in one package.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes an integrated Django authentication app that handles both local accounts and social authentication under one set of flows. Local login can use username or email, with verification strategies ranging from none to mandatory email verification. Social login supports any OpenID Connect-compatible provider, many OAuth 1.0/2.0 providers, SAML 2.0, and custom protocols such as Telegram. It enables rate limiting by default and offers account enumeration prevention so users cannot tell whether an email already has an account. Consumer keys and secrets can be set in regular settings or in the database through the Django admin, with optional support for the Django sites framework.
use_cases: add user registration and login to a Django site
let users sign in with Google, Facebook, or X accounts
single sign-on with SAML 2.0 for B2B customers
require email verification for new accounts
manage social provider keys from the Django admin
notable: Unifies local login and social login in one app, avoiding the gap between separate packages
Supports OpenID Connect, many OAuth 1.0/2.0 providers, SAML 2.0, and Telegram login
Rate limiting and account enumeration prevention enabled out of the box
Provider credentials configurable via settings or the Django admin
caveats: The README gives no install or run commands in the provided excerpt, so setup details must be taken from the full documentation
Commercial support is offered by a separate vendor, implying advanced help is not free
